# Problem 1
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Default setup
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_colour_viridis_d
scale_fill_discrete = scale_fill_viridis_d
```

## Loading the dataset
```{r}
data("ny_noaa")
```

## EDA
```{r}
dimension = dim(ny_noaa)
stationcount = n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)
daterange = range(ny_noaa$date)

ny_noaa |>
  summarize(across(everything(), \(x) mean(is.na(x)))) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The ny_noaa dataset has 2595176 rows and 7 columns. It includes the following variables: `r colnames(ny_noaa)`. The data is from `r stationcount` distinct stations with date in the range of `r daterange`. A considerable amount of data is missing. Specifically, 43.7% of tmax and tmin values are not available. In addition, some proportion of snowfall, snow depth and precipitation data are also missing.

## Data cleaning
```{r}
ny_noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )

ny_noaa_df |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE)
```

The most commonly observed snowfall value is 0. This is potentially because that it does not snow on most days of the year. After 0, the most common values are NA, 25, 13, and 51 mm.

## Two-panel plot showing the average max temperature in January and in July in each station across years
```{r}
ny_noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  mutate(month = month.name[month]) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(. ~ month)
```

From the plot, the average max temperatures for January and July are around 0 and 27 degrees respectively. The values varies more in January than in July. There are two most obvious outliers, with one station observing about 14 degress in July and another observing about -13 degrees in January.

## Two-panel plot showing tmax vs tmin
```{r}
ny_noaa_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d()
```

According to the plot, tmax and tmin are positively related. The dense cluster in the middle suggests that tmax is about 10-15 degress higher than tmin in most of the days.

## Plot showing the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 separately by year
```{r}
ny_noaa_df |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_violin()
```

From the plot, the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 demonstrate similar trend over the years.

# Problem 2
## Data cleaning and merging
```{r}
demo_df = 
  read_csv("data/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4) |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    sex = case_match(
      sex, 
      1 ~ "male", 
      2 ~ "female"
      ),
    education = case_match(
      education,
      1 ~ "Less than high school",
      2 ~ "High school equivalent",
      3 ~ "More than high school"
    )
  )

acc_df =
  read_csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims"
  )

nhanes_df =
  left_join(demo_df, acc_df, by = "seqn")
```

## Table for the number of men and women in each education category
```{r}
demo_df |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Age distributions for men and women in each education category
```{r}
demo_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = education, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

## Creating a total activity variable for each participant
```{r}
total_df =
  nhanes_df |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) |>
  summarize(total_mims = sum(mims))
```
## Comparing total activities for "Less than high school" group
```{r}
total_df |>
  filter(education == "Less than high school") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

## Comparing total activities for "High school equivalent" group
```{r}
total_df |>
  filter(education == "High school equivalent") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

## Comparing total activities for "More than high school" group
```{r}
total_df |>
  filter(education == "More than high school") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

## Three-panel plot that shows the 24-hour activity time courses for "Less than high school" group
```{r}
nhanes_df |>
  filter(education == "Less than high school") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = minute, y = mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = seqn), alpha = .1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

## Three-panel plot that shows the 24-hour activity time courses for "High school equivalent" group
```{r}
nhanes_df |>
  filter(education == "High school equivalent") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = minute, y = mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = seqn), alpha = .1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

## Three-panel plot that shows the 24-hour activity time courses for "More than high school" group
```{r}
nhanes_df |>
  filter(education == "More than high school") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = minute, y = mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = seqn), alpha = .1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

# Problem 3
## Importing and cleaning the datasets
```{r}
jan_2020_df =
  read_csv("data/citibike/Jan 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  mutate(year = 2020, month = "January")

july_2020_df =
  read_csv("data/citibike/July 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  mutate(year = 2020, month = "July")

jan_2024_df =
  read_csv("data/citibike/Jan 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  mutate(year = 2024, month = "January")

july_2024_df =
  read_csv("data/citibike/July 2024 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  mutate(year = 2024, month = "July")
```

## Total number of rides in each combination of year and month separating casual riders and Citi Bike members
```{r}
bind_rows(jan_2020_df, july_2020_df, jan_2024_df, july_2024_df) |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Table showing the 5 most popular starting stations for July 2024
```{r}
july_2024_df |>
  count(start_station_name) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  head(5) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Investigating the effects of day of the week, month, and year on median ride duration
```{r}
median_df =
  bind_rows(jan_2020_df, july_2020_df, jan_2024_df, july_2024_df) |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(median_duration = median(duration)) |>
  mutate(year = as.character(year))

median_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekdays, y = median_duration, color = month, shape = year)) +
  geom_point()
```

## Impact of month, membership status, and bike type on the distribution of ride duration
```{r}
bind_rows(jan_2024_df, july_2024_df) |>
  mutate(rider_bike = paste(member_casual, rideable_type)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = duration, y = rider_bike, fill = month)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
